title: Optimal Management of Welding Quality of Wind Power Tower Based on AHP and PDCA Cycle
content: Background: Wind power tower welding quality is crucial for ensuring the safety and reliability of wind energy infrastructure. However, current welding quality control methods face challenges in effectively managing the complex factors involved. This study aims to develop an optimal welding quality management approach for wind power towers by integrating the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) and the Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA) cycle. Methods: The proposed approach utilizes AHP to identify and prioritize critical welding quality factors, while the PDCA cycle is employed for continuous improvement of welding processes. The integration of these two methods enables a comprehensive and systematic approach to welding quality management. Results: The study identifies the most critical welding quality factors using AHP and demonstrates the successful implementation of the PDCA cycle for welding quality improvement. Conclusion: The integration of AHP and PDCA cycle provides an optimal approach for managing welding quality in wind power tower manufacturing. The findings of this study have significant implications for enhancing the safety, reliability, and efficiency of wind energy infrastructure. Further research and application of this approach are recommended to drive continuous improvement in welding quality management practices.
